most_likely: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma, precipitated by insulin nonadherence
summary: Young woman with long-standing poorly controlled type 1 diabetes and multiple prior DKA episodes, now 5 weeks postpartum (infant in NICU), admitted to the ICU with severe DKA: glucose 854, HCO3 3, anion gap 36, pH 6.96, with concomitant lactic acidosis (lactate 3.6–5.4) and marked electrolyte derangement (K 8.8, Phos 7.1, Mg 7.4, transient Cr 1.4). Precipitant was medication nonadherence/running out of insulin in the setting of social stress; no infectious source identified (clear CXR, no pneumonia, negative UE ultrasound, head CT normal). She improved on insulin infusion and fluids, transferred to medicine, and pelvic ultrasound for persistent postpartum bleeding showed only intracavitary blood products without retained products of conception.
